facts.statement: The researchers used live electrical recording methods to study the spinal cord of mice with a specific model of atopic dermatitis.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Mice with the atopic dermatitis model showed spontaneous electrical activity in their spinal cords that was not seen in healthy control mice.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The spontaneous electrical activity stopped when a drug blocking glutamate receptors was applied, but it did not stop when drugs blocking gastrin-releasing peptide or natriuretic peptide receptors were used.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Detailed electrical measurements showed that neurons in the spinal cords of the atopic dermatitis mice had more excitatory signals and fewer inhibitory signals than normal.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Tests of the spinal cord tissue found higher levels of gastrin-releasing peptide and a marker for a type of immune cell called microglia in the atopic dermatitis mice.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The authors suggest that an imbalance between excitatory and inhibitory signals in the spinal cord contributes to the heightened sensitivity to itch seen in this chronic condition.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The authors state that this is the first study to directly show changes in the balance of excitatory and inhibitory signals in a mouse model of chronic itch.
facts.subject: animals
